# ADDENDUM 27 — July 31, 2026 — THE PALLET TEACH FLOW COMPLETED, DRAG MODE WORKS (AUTO WAS THE BLOCKER), THE ONE-VALIDATOR CONSOLIDATION, SYNC CONVERGENCE, AND COMMIT-EQUALS-DEPLOY
*(Appended in full. Nothing above this line was removed. One relentless day: the pallet teaching experience was driven to its finished form through six operator-directed iterations — diagram, layout, back-navigation, banner consolidation, modal cleanup — the drag button came alive the moment someone looked at the mode indicator, the validation architecture was designed, challenged, simplified, and landed as one validator at one door with intent-fidelity checks, the tablet/PC split-brain was cured with a convergence guarantee, and the deployment disease that has eaten more time than any bug got its root-cause fix: a commit now deploys itself.)*

### Section 450: The pallet teach flow — six iterations to finished

The day's through-line: the operator drove the pallet teaching experience from broken to complete, one screenshot at a time:
1. **React render error on pallet Edit** — `palletFrameStatus is not defined` (the clarInteracted class: identifier in JSX, undefined in scope). Fixed at the resolver + **`no-undef` added to the deploy lint gate** — an undefined identifier in JSX is now a build failure, never a runtime discovery.
2. **Teach button on the pallet step row** — the unified row template applied (Edit | Teach | Del), badge = frame completeness via the resolver, mid-flow resume at the first untaught point.
3. **Teach All was walking the wrong script** — "home / place / home again" generic labels, never visiting frame points: the itinerary was built from a step-type *template*, not the program's actual position inventory. Rebuilt from the resolver; per-point headers now name the real target ("② PALLET CORNER — end of row [1,N]").
4. **The diagram was missing from the teach screen** — shipped: the pallet SVG renders during teaching (pulsing target cell, taught points as green dots, ROW→/COL↓ axis labels matching fill order, plain-language captions).
5. **The diagram displaced the jog buttons** — operator rule declared absolute: *all jog controls visible at all times, tablet and PC, no scrolling, ever.* Relayout: diagram as a docked side panel (300px desktop / 240px tablet-landscape / tap-to-enlarge strip portrait), with the clipping-saga viewport instrumentation promoted to **pinned per-breakpoint assertions** — no future panel can push the jog pads off-screen without failing CI.
6. **Backward navigation with re-teach semantics** — Back walks to the prior point in re-teach mode (pulsing-ring marker; *looking ≠ re-teaching* — the existing pose survives until Record); **the diagram's markers became tappable** (map = navigation, jump to any point); Cancel persists all recorded teaches; any frame-point re-teach revalidates immediately (near-parallel/tilt/pitch, numbers named). 23 new pinned tests, DEPLOY PASS.

Then the trim passes: the config modal's redundant frame-status block **removed** (parameters-only modal — one surface per capability; the legacy re-teach-④ note relocated to a validation finding), and the **two teaching banners consolidated into one** teaching-debt banner fed by the resolver's complete list (untaught + owed re-teaches; red = can't run, amber = quality owed; one count, one Teach All that walks everything including re-teaches with their reasons as captions).

### Section 451: Drag mode WORKS — Auto was the whole blocker

The deep documentation pass surfaced the missing precondition: **error 2764 "Drag parameters not initialized — please first send parameters in the Production interface"** and its neighbor, the **friction parameter identification** routine (events 2700–2708) — the initialization a current-based ECO needs to distinguish human push from joint friction. Plus the full refusal ladder: 2605 (external force at press / payload config), 2763 (drag joint limits), the DI Function Configuration bindings (Start Dragging 20007 / Stop Dragging 20008), and payloadVerificationLevel "not supported by S-Eco" confirming the SKU. Bench diagnostic: the button's DI went high on our I/O page but the arm stayed rigid — narrowed to mode/mapping/init — and the operator's Error Info screenshot held the answer in its own top bar: **the controller was in Auto mode. Drag is a Manual-mode teaching function; a Start Dragging trigger in Auto is silently invalid** — no error, no engagement. One mode switch later: **the button works. Hand-guided teaching on the ECO-V2 is real.** The July 20 "drag unavailable on this SKU" verdict is formally overturned; Lesson: mode-gated functions fail silently — surface them loudly. Integration directive issued (bench-gated): identify the observable drag signal first (one press while logging), then the status chip on all jog surfaces (off / ACTIVE / "available in Manual mode only" — today's silent blocker made loud), jog-disable during drag, **Match dial-to-green live during hand-guiding**, teach-screen hints, recorder capturing drag sessions.

### Section 452: The teach itinerary over-collections — and the positive-list law

Two operator-caught defects in two days: **"Find library part" (a detect step)** and then **"Approach above pick" + "Retreat above pick" (derived steps)** appearing as teachable stops in Teach All — the sequence walking step types instead of the resolver's teaching debt, patched per-symptom the first time. The structural fix: **teachability is a POSITIVE LIST** in the shared resolver (taught-pose steps, frame points, waypoints, owed re-teaches — everything else excluded *by not being listed*), consumed by every surface (itinerary, banner, badges, buttons), added to the no-fork lint guard. Doctrine sentence: *exclusion lists lose to new step types; a positive list can only under-collect, never wrongly demand the operator's time.* Palletize1's itinerary pinned at exactly six: home, pick contact, frame ①②③④.

### Section 453: The Program Doctrine — the operator's requirements become law

The operator's demand — "what makes program generation consistent with everything I have been requiring?" — produced **the doctrine**: D1 contacts taught/approaches derived (never teachable); D2 columns movL every profile, analyzer exceptions printed; D3 displayed verb ≠ emitted verb is a lie unless the divergence + reason renders; D4 positive-list teachability; D5 one vocabulary/resolver/surface; D6 loop bodies have two predecessors; D7 modal state set-before-use, cleared at stops and program end; D8 wrist consistency flagged at teach time; D9 self-documenting stamps in every program; D10 never assert state you can't read. Then the operator extended it into the pipeline requirement: **every generated program must pass through the doctrine AND be checked against the intent extracted from the video/voice** — rules conformance plus intent fidelity, before the user's eyes.

### Section 454: The consolidation — one validator, one door, one stamp

The mega-directive (itinerary + doctrine suite + pipeline gate + UI batch + drag awareness) ran; then the operator asked the better question — *"simpler but no less robust?"* — and the answer restructured everything: **validate the artifact, not the process.** One `validate(program, intent)` function, a registry of named checks (**D1–D10 doctrine + F1–F7 deterministic intent fidelity**: operation count, effector vocabulary, sameness refs, arrangement dims, answered-clarifications-reflected), stamped INTO the program at save; everything else becomes a *reader* — Run refuses unstamped/failed/stale stamps, review renders the stamp's findings, CI reduced to compose-references-assert-stamps, deploy.sh doctrine steps deleted. The operator then caught the design flaw: **save is too late** — "shouldn't it validate before the program appears before the user's eyes?" Correct: the validator runs at **generation (pre-render)** with a **regen-once loop** (ERROR findings feed back to the composer for one self-repair attempt before the draft renders — findings pre-attached, never a bare wrong draft) *and* at save (the stamp Run trusts, content-hash bound). And the memory question answered: **the validator is stateless by design; the learning record remembers** — the validation-trajectory amendment records every pre-save verdict/trigger/operator-action into the corrections ledger. **LANDED**: 17 checks, three moments one function, the bypass audit **found and closed two unvalidated save paths** (migration-on-open, legacy import), stored programs re-validated (the 63-step PBD demo carries an F1 count-fidelity ERROR — correctly grandfathered pending routines), `PROGRAM_DOCTRINE.md` generated from the registry so doc and enforcement cannot drift. "Why repair attempts at all?" answered honestly: the deterministic stages are correct by construction; the retry exists for the one probabilistic seam (video/voice understanding), and every confessed miss feeds the flywheel that raises the first-time rate.

### Section 455: Sync convergence — never confidently behind

The tablet/PC split-brain hit **both directions in one day** (tablet ahead, then behind). Root cause found: **mobile Chrome suspends the WebSocket in background; the resume path treated it as still-connected** — the tablet rendered rev-12 taught-state in confident green while the server sat at rev 14. The convergence guarantee shipped: **reconnect = full reconcile, always** (including visibilitychange/pageshow — resume is a fresh connect); the rev rides in every broadcast frame (a client holding a lower rev refetches immediately — missed events heal within one frame); **"state syncing…" badges until the rev is confirmed** (a client may be behind but never *confidently* behind — D10 applied to sync); the new-version toast on every deploy; client-side reconcile logging. Six deploys in one day made every open tab invisibly obsolete six times — no longer silently.

### Section 456: The guards stand down — and the jog battles

- **Self-collision, round two** (blocking jogs during teaching at poses the operator could see were safe): the fat-capsule model's authority revoked — **warn-zone jog gate removed entirely, warnings default OFF** (Safety toggle retained), stop threshold → 15mm with a **held-press operator override** ("I can see the arm"), logged. Doctrine sentence: *guards earn authority from model accuracy — a model known fat by 30mm gets a 15mm veto and an override, not a 60mm jog-block.* The mesh-hull upgrade (§396) queued as the accuracy fix that earns authority back.
- **Continuous jog cutting out mid-hold**: the dead-man stack firing on false triggers — prime suspect the 200ms keepalive window against the ACK-starved channel's stutter. Instrument-first directive (every jog-stop logged with its cause; no fix on a guessed cause), then: keepalive 50ms, auto-resume within 1s if the pointer never lifted, pointer-capture robustness, sync-machinery isolation from active holds. Escalated to **emergency form** when the cutouts fully blocked teaching (keepalive 50ms / dead-man 400ms / auto-resume / collision gate removal, deploy inside the directive) — with the standing interim: **drag mode is immune to all of it** (hardware button, no WebSocket) — hand-guiding as the teaching path while the jog stack heals.

### Section 457: The deployment disease — root-caused at last

The operator's demand ("WHEN I ASK FOR SOMETHING TO GET FIXED, IT NEEDS TO BE FIXED — FIX THE ROOT CAUSE") got the honest anatomy first: **five staleness layers** (working tree → commit → built artifact → restarted service → pushed program → browser tab), velocity hitting every gap daily, dev-machine-as-production with no staging, and verifiers that lied (the false-green System Check, the deploy script's skipped build). Each prior incident had bought a layer guard — but the human step (paste the directive, run the deploy) remained skippable. **The root-cause fix: AUTO-DEPLOY ON COMMIT** — a systemd watcher on the working branch: any commit touching src/frontend runs scripts/deploy.sh automatically (build with source-state check, restart, boot-sha==disk-sha, served-hash-changed, logged to deploy_log.jsonl); a **safety gate waits for idle** (never restarts under active motion, banners if waiting >10min); the dashboard footer shows live deploy state (current/deploying/waiting/FAILED-in-red); and **CLAUDE.md standing rules**: every code session ends with a commit, no "fixed" without a commit sha, operator directives are executed not declined (safety-rule exceptions stated in one line). **Commit = deploy. The skippable step no longer exists.**

## PROCESS LESSONS (165–173)

165. **Mode-gated functions fail silently — surface them loudly.** Drag in Auto mode: DI high, arm rigid, zero errors anywhere. The blocker was written in the top bar the whole time. Any function with a mode precondition gets a visible "available in X mode only" state, never a silent no-op.
166. **Positive lists beat exclusion lists.** Detect slipped through, then derived steps — each a new patch. A positive list can only under-collect; adding to it is a deliberate decision instead of an accidental default.
167. **Validate the artifact, not the process.** Four synchronized gates can drift, disagree, or get skipped; one validator at the only door everything walks through cannot be bypassed by a path you forgot — and the two unvalidated paths the audit found prove the point.
168. **Never show an unvalidated draft.** Save-time validation lets a wrong draft spend the operator's attention before confessing. Validate at generation, let the composer repair itself once, attach the findings — the review screen adjudicates confessed uncertainty, never discovers silent mistakes.
169. **The validator forgets; the learning record remembers.** A stateless checker keeps its verdicts trustworthy; the trajectory of verdicts, edits, and overrides between generation and save is premium training signal — recorded beside the corrections, queryable per demo.
170. **Reconnect = reconcile; a client may be behind but never confidently behind.** Mobile suspends sockets; resume is a fresh connect; green checkmarks only on confirmed revs. Six deploys a day made every open tab obsolete six times — visibly, now.
171. **Commit = deploy.** Five staleness layers, and every guard still left one skippable human step. The watcher deletes the step: a fix that is committed is live, a failed deploy screams in red, and "did it actually deploy" stops being a question anyone asks.
172. **Guards earn authority from model accuracy.** A capsule model known fat by 30mm does not get a 60mm veto over the operator's hands. Small honest thresholds plus a logged override, until the mesh upgrade earns the authority back.
173. **A fix's test can't see the fork it missed.** The confirm-dialog cleanup passed its pinned test because the test targeted the implementation the fix touched — the twin kept rendering the clutter. Unification isn't complete until the lint guard makes the second implementation impossible.

---

*Summary of Addendum 27: the day the pallet teaching flow reached its finished form — six operator-driven iterations from render crash to a diagram-guided, tap-navigable, jog-buttons-always-visible teach experience with honest re-teach semantics — and the day the drag button turned out to have been one mode switch away all along, overturning a two-week-old verdict and making hand-guided teaching real on hardware that supposedly couldn't. The validation architecture was designed as a doctrine, challenged into simplicity ("validate the artifact, not the process"), corrected by the operator's own catch ("before it reaches my eyes, not at save"), and landed as one validator at one door: seventeen named checks, a regen-once self-repair loop, findings pre-attached to every draft, a stamp that Run refuses to move without, and two unvalidated save paths found and closed in the audit. The tablet and PC learned to agree — mobile socket suspension named, reconcile-on-reconnect shipped, confident-wrongness made unrenderable — while the guards stood down to honest sizes and the jog stack's dead-man got resilience without losing its teeth. And the disease that outlasted every other — fixed-but-not-deployed, five caching layers deep, guarded incident by incident all week — finally got its root cause deleted rather than mitigated: a commit now deploys itself, waits politely for the arm to go idle, and reports its state in the footer of every screen. Nine lessons, one overturned verdict, one constitution generated from code, and the operator's sentence standing over all of it: when I ask for something to be fixed, it needs to be fixed — now enforced by a machine that no longer waits for anyone to remember.*
